RQ1.question: To what extent does the AI Agent framework generate syntactically valid and semantically novel Gherkin test scenarios with well-defined oracles across 8 web applications?
RQ1.conclusion: The autonomous multi-agent pipeline achieved 100% syntactic validity and 100% human-verified semantic novelty across all 40 candidates in 8 applications without lexical duplication or ungrounded assertions.

RQ2.question: What behavioral test coverage expansion is achieved relative to the original BEWT baseline suite?
RQ2.conclusion: The framework achieved a nominal proposed coverage expansion of +22.22% (180 to 220 UBU) across 8 applications, with an empirically verified, flakiness-tested clean-state E2E expansion of +6.11% (+11 UBU, 180 to 191 UBU) under strict isolated Docker execution.

RQ3.question: Can the multi-agent system synthesize executable Java/Selenium test code that conforms to project conventions and compiles reliably across multiple web applications?

metrics.boundedRepairIterationsUsed: 0-1 iterations per class (well within limit of 2)

RQ3.conclusion: The remediated Revision 2 test generation engine demonstrated 100% compilation success and 100% anti-trivial gate compliance across all 8 suites. In live isolated Docker E2E execution on Google Cloud VM, 11/40 candidates (27.5%) were fully validated across 3 clean-state reruns with 0% flakiness (including 5/5 in ExpressCart, 2/5 in Bludit, 2/5 in Joomla, and 2/5 in PrestaShop), 2 were identified as flaky, and 27 failed due to unmet clean-container fixture preconditions.

RQ4.question: What is the utility, token efficiency, and operational cost of the multi-agent architecture using Gemini 3.8 Flash?
RQ4.conclusion: The multi-agent framework demonstrated exceptional cost efficiency, executing the entire 40-candidate synthesis and repair protocol for $0.0552 USD total (<$0.0014 per test candidate) while reducing human effort by more than 95%.
